- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 90+ → 92+), then sharply correct downward.
- Mean reversion is strong in the final 5–10 days of the forecast; model fails to reflect this, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price drops — underestimates when prices fall sharply from prior peaks.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 3–5 days, especially when history shows recent volatility or downward momentum.
- Model fails to adjust for downward momentum in the last 5–10 days of history — often underestimates the depth of the drop.
- When history shows a clear downward trend, model tends to ignore it and forecasts higher than true outcome.
- Forecasts are sensitive to recent high prices — model often assumes continuation of upward trend even when evidence suggests reversal.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price drops after a spike — especially in the 10–20 day window.
- Model overestimates the persistence of upward momentum — fails to recognize that price corrections are often faster than modeled.
